subject: JaxSel status: pathfinder baseline in, selection sparsity trade-off
body:
Hi Anders, Alina,

Status. The May 22 milestone landed a bit late (May 28) but we now match the pathfinder numbers from the long-range-arena setup within noise, and it's wired into CI as a regression gate.

The interesting finding is a trade-off in the selection layer. Because the Agent model estimates edge weights from purely local features, tightening the sparsity budget below ~400 nodes per extracted subgraph starts dropping the long-range connections pathfinder specifically needs — we lose 6.1 points of classification accuracy at the 256-node budget versus 512. On the 10M-node synthetic graph the story is better: task-relevant neighborhoods are shallower, and a 512-node budget holds accuracy while keeping extraction under 180ms.

Risk to flag: gradient variance through the sparse PageRank iteration grows with graph diameter. Nikhil has a damping tweak in review. If it doesn't hold we may need to cap supported diameter for v1.

Rafael
